questions.q: Explain Mendel's monohybrid cross and the conclusions drawn from it.

answer.text: Gregor Mendel crossed pure tall pea plants with pure short pea plants. In the first generation, called F1, all the plants were tall, and the short character seemed to disappear.
When these F1 tall plants were self-pollinated, the second generation, called F2, contained both tall and short plants in the ratio of three tall to one short. The short trait had reappeared.

Mendel concluded that traits are controlled by factors, now called genes, which occur in pairs. When two different forms are present, one, the dominant, is expressed while the other, the recessive, is hidden. In F2 the recessive short trait reappeared, showing that it had merely been masked, not lost.

answer: These experiments laid the foundation of the science of genetics.

questions.q: How is the sex of a child determined in human beings?

answer.text: Human beings have 23 pairs of chromosomes, of which one pair are the sex chromosomes. Females have two X chromosomes, written as XX, while males have one X and one Y chromosome, written as XY.
When gametes are formed, every egg produced by the mother carries an X chromosome. The father, however, produces two kinds of sperm, half carrying an X chromosome and half carrying a Y chromosome.

If a sperm carrying X fertilises the egg, the child is XX, a girl. If a sperm carrying Y fertilises the egg, the child is XY, a boy. So it is the type of sperm from the father that decides the sex of the child.

answer: This shows that the father, not the mother, determines the sex of the child.
